newsitem.title: IRAQ: Egyptian firms in Baghdad to sell food, medicine.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian firms in Baghdad to sell food, medicine.

text.p: Twenty-six Egyptian companies opened a trade exhibition in Baghdad on Saturday, seeking deals to sell millions of dollars worth of food and medical products when an oil-for-food deal with the U.N. takes effect.

"We hope that we will be able to sign contracts with Iraqi traders and government establishments to bring foodstuffs and medicine in accordance with the United Nations resolutions," said Assam al-Khashab, head of representatives of the Egyptian firms attending the fair.

Iraq and the United Nations signed an agreement in May allowing Iraq oil sales worth $2 billion every six months to buy food and medicine for its people, suffering from stringent U.N. trade sanctions for the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The implementation of the deal, which was expected in September, stalled after Baghdad forces intervened in inter-Kurdish fighting in northern Iraq in late August.
